name: Baron Falls Tower
text: [overview] Descend the couloir full of snow on the climbers right side.

name: Chockstone Couloir
text: [overview] depending on season it is passed on mixed ground of stone, ice and snow, or surmounted head-on at 5.4.
[overview] Snow is 40 degrees below it and 50 above, with short 55 degree rolls.
[detailed_rack] Two pickets and a light rack for alpine routes.
[detailed_rack] A bolted belay on the right is often snow-covered.

name: Cowboy Poetry
text: [detailed_rack] Cams in small to medium sizes, short ice screws, a snow anchor such as a picket or pig, and plenty of knife blades and bugaboo pins.

name: East Ridge
text: [obj_haz] Early- or late-season snow and ice on the ridge.
[detailed_rack] Winter: ice axe, snow anchors, ropes, harnesses;

name: North Face of Mount Borah
text: [overview] It can be a snow climb in early summer once avalanche danger subsides, but is best in early fall, when ice builds up in many beautiful alpine pitches.
[overview] Above the first snow or scree, several options exist for passing the band of rock lower down;
[overview] Next come a higher expanse of snow and ice, then the summit headwall.

name: Left Ventricle
text: [overview] Leave the snow field called the Heart and enter the left chimney.
[overview] Expect snow features, chalkstones, and steps that mix vertical ice with rock.
[overview] Near the top the chimney opens onto a wide snowfield, where you head for the bottom of a big inverted cone and pass it on its left.
[overview] A big cornice may form up top.

[approach] One follows the standard route up the neighbouring peak past the ridge crux to the saddle below its final climb, then drops east from the north end of the saddle over scree or snow until below the face;
[approach] Left Ventricle starts from the snowfield in the heart-shaped bowl and enters a chimney on the left.

name: Right Ventricle
text: [overview] Go up the snow apron under it, through a tight rock gap, into the bowl, then up and right to the narrow couloir.
[overview] Several hundred feet of steep snow and styrofoam or alpine ice follow;
[overview] At its end is a narrow chimney hopefully holding water ice, climbed to another chockstone, and steep snow gets you to the ridge.

[approach] One follows the standard route up the neighbouring peak past the ridge crux to the saddle below its final climb, then drops east from the north end of the saddle over scree or snow until below the face;

[approach] Right Ventricle starts on the snow apron below the heart-shaped bowl on the eastern part of the face: pass through a narrow rock gap into the bowl, then head up and right to the narrow couloir that begins the route.

name: Agri-Alpinism
text: [overview] P7-8: easy snow couloir, then a moderate, exposed pitch of mixed climbing.

name: Breakfast Scramble
text: [overview] It starts up Alpine Simulator's first pitch, then continues up a tight gully through several constrictions to a ramp of snow and ice leading to the summit.
[overview] Conditions matter a lot: snow can be sugary in some years, and heavy snow years bury most of the ice.
[overview] Easiest descent is the gully on climbers right at the top, glissading and scrambling, around 15 minutes.

name: Ghetto Simulator
text: [overview] A sensible route through the middle of the small buttress shaped like a triangle, west of the Alpine Simulator one, with a snow couloir on each side, then an easier couloir angling west to east toward the summit.
[overview] P2 (M4+): snow ramp, easy chimney, then the crux corner with steep cracks and a tight, awkward slot holding a recently fixed pin.
[overview] P3: scramble, then a rope length of steep snow.
[overview] P4: snow or M2.
[overview] P5-6 (snow/M4): chimney with an awkward chockstone move, then juggy exposed slabs.
[approach] The route takes the little triangular buttress that sits west of the Alpine Simulator one, with a snow couloir on each side, and lies right of Fear Machine.

name: South Couloir
text: [beta] this slot often holds snow late into summer.
[hazards] Snow-filled headwall below the Thompson-Williams saddle.
[obj_haz] Firm early-season snow on steep slopes.
[gear] Ice axe and microspikes or crampons early season or when the headwall holds snow
[descent_text] Take care finding the correct break in the headwall on the way down, especially if it is snow-filled.
[turnaround] Turn back if the headwall below the saddle is hard snow or ice and you have no axe and traction, or if thunderstorms are building by early afternoon;
[pitch_detail] Often snow-filled well into summer..
[pro_tips] Go mid-July or later for a snow-free headwall.
